config._note: humaniq-dashboard-steering-indicators replaces the prior 15-widget queue-depth Dashboard (12 stat tiles + 3 object-table lists) with 6 steering indicators. Billable ratio and Headcount & turnover bind via dataSource (raw GraphQL, no new backend endpoint, unguarded — the same exposure every Employees/Timesheets index page already has today); the filter/tenant-scoping token grammar (`@workspace.activeAdministrationId?`) does NOT apply to the raw-GraphQL dataSource form (`useDataSource.js`'s `queryAndVars` passes `graphql.query`/`graphql.variables` through unresolved — confirmed by reading the composable, both in the sibling source tree and the installed dist), so these two widgets are UNSCOPED across administrations rather than carrying the (broken, per brief §6) sentinel token — no worse than today's index-page exposure, but not literally what design.md D4 describes either. Both are also single-series, not the two-named-series design.md's D1 table describes: `useDataSource`'s raw-GraphQL `selectors` map performs one dot-path pluck per output key (`selectByPath` in `useGraphQL.js`) with no mechanism to assemble two differently-aliased root fields into one `[{name,data}]` series array — verified against the installed dist, not just the source tree. Absence rate / Payroll cost per period / Approval lead time bind via `endpointSource` to the new guarded `AnalyticsController::trends()` (REQ-DSI-004/006/007); Obligations binds via `endpointSource` to `AnalyticsController::obligations()` (REQ-DSI-008/009). All three trend `endpointSource` widgets go through the local `chart` widgetKey override (`registry.js` → `src/widgets/TrendChartWidget.vue`), which does its OWN null-safe series mapping rather than delegating to CnChartWidget's native `endpointSource` prop — that prop's own `Number(value) || 0` mapping (`CnChartWidget.vue`'s `endpointChartData`, confirmed in the installed dist) silently turns a `null` bucket into `0`, which is exactly the 'measurement that never ran reads as a good result' failure REQ-DSI-004's null-not-zero contract exists to prevent. The `chart` widgetKey is ALSO overridden for a second, independent reason: CnChartWidget (registered in the library's dashboard-widget catalog) was built to be embedded inside CnDashboardPage's own per-widget template, which supplies the title bar externally — it has no `title` prop and does not self-wrap in CnWidgetWrapper, and `CnWidgetGrid` (the only renderer humaniq's pages use, since every page has a `slot:"body"` widget) mounts it bare. `TrendChartWidget.vue` bridges both gaps — the SAME `effectiveRegistry`-wins-over-catalog mechanism `registry.js` already uses for `stat`, and the same bridge-a-mismatched-library-component pattern already used for `actions`/`lifecycle-actions`. The Obligations `object-table` widget uses CnWidgetObjectTable's REAL flat prop names directly (`endpointSource`/`columns`/`emptyText`, siblings of `title` under `props`) rather than nesting them under a `content` key the way the removed 'Aflopende contracten'/'Aflopende BHV-certificaten' widgets did — CnWidgetObjectTable declares no `content` prop (confirmed in both the source tree and the installed dist), so that nested shape would not have reached the component; a per-row route to each obligation's own detail page (SickLeaveCaseDetail/EmploymentContractDetail/BhvCertificeringDetail, varying by row TYPE) is not wired: CnWidgetObjectTable's `rowRoute` is a single STATIC route-name string for the whole table, not a per-row dynamic selector, so the endpoint's own per-row `route` field is carried in the response but not yet clickable from this widget.

config._note: hrmq-personal-dashboard (design.md D1/D3): the caller-scoped personal landing surface hydra ADR-097 Decision 3 requires — 'route to a type: "dashboard" page scoped to the caller … Not an index page, and not a bare parent with no route of its own'. The MijnHrGroup menu entry gains route: "MijnHr" through this fragment's menu block (mergeMenuItems fills the base group's undefined route key), so the group title lands here while its nine children stay under the collapse chevron — both of Decision 3's conditions, which moves humaniq's counted main-menu total from 6 to 5. Every widget carries a caller-scope filter (userId: "@me", or managerUserId: "@me" for the approver's own queue) plus the OPTIONAL administration token @workspace.activeAdministrationId? — unresolved means dropped, so a widget degrades to user-scoped-only, never to another user's rows. Only the built-in `stat` and `object-table` types are used (stat resolves through humaniq's own registry.js override, which is load-bearing: the library's self-registration is tree-shaken out of the production bundle); no custom widget, no new backend endpoint, no raw-GraphQL dataSource (the steering Dashboard's _note documents why that form resolves a schema by name across every register on the instance). Widget 6 has no conditional-visibility primitive available — the dashboard widget grammar has none for stat tiles (design.md D4) — so it always renders and shows 0 for a caller who manages nobody; its caption keeps the zero legible. The stat tiles' click-through uses content.route in the vue-router LOCATION-OBJECT form ({"name": "…"}), not the bare string design.md D3 writes: widgetLink passes a string straight to <router-link :to>, where vue-router 4 reads it as a PATH, so a bare route NAME would fall through to the catch-all. Same spelling the hr-objects nav-card entries already use. The three object-table widgets carry the FLAT content contract (register/schema/filter/sort{field,dir}/limit/columns/rowRoute/viewAllRoute/emptyText), NOT the nested `source` shape design.md D3 writes — measured live 2026-08-22, not inferred: on a type:"dashboard" page CnDashboardPage.registryRenderer looks up getWidgetTypeEntry(canonicalWidgetType(type)), and utils/widgetTypeAliases.js maps `object-table` -> `table`, which registerDashboardWidgets.js registers INLINE to CnObjectListWidget. The alias therefore never reaches CnWidgetObjectTable's dashboardRegistration (its `object-table` key is registered under a name the canonicaliser has already rewritten away, in a side-effect module ADR-061 tree-shaking drops anyway). With the `source` shape the widget rendered its emptyText and fired ZERO fetches, because CnObjectListWidget reads content.register/content.schema and has no `source` key at all. Consequences of the real contract, accepted: `limit` is a FETCH CAP (ADR-062), not a render promise — the visible row count fits the cell — and there is no per-row-route escape, which is fine since rowRoute is already a single static route name. All three also carry allowCreate: false — CnObjectListWidget renders a "+ Toevoegen" create affordance by DEFAULT (measured live), and all three collections are read-only to the employee: Timesheets are server-created by the booking flow (MijnUrenstaten already sets showAdd: false), LeaveBalance is written only by LeaveAccrualJob, and payslips are payroll-generated (REQ-MHS-004's read-only posture). Labels are Dutch literals; hrmq-i18n-locale-completeness owns their conversion and this change adds no English keys. self-service-announcements-and-digest (2026-09-30): the Announcements table on top is the one exception to no new endpoint: it reads GET /api/announcements/mine, because an audience of one of my departments is not a declarative filter (design D2).

working-hours-per-person (2026-09-18): the third kind of absence (design.md D3). Leave is requested and drawn from a balance (LeaveRequests), sickness is a case with a poortwachter timeline (SickLeaveCases), and this is neither: nothing is requested and no balance moves. The reason list is administered and holds no leave type, so a row here can never read as verlof on a day the person was never contracted to work.

store._note: Configuration exchange, not rows. A configuration set carries the registers, schemas, objects, views, flows, sources and mappings that make one way of working hold together. There is deliberately NO `installable` allowlist: a set exists to introduce schemas the instance does not have YET, so listing schemas this app already owns would refuse exactly the sets worth installing. The trust boundary for a bundle is its publisher, enforced by the engine's source allowlist and trusted-key check. ⚠️ An EMPTY `installable` means install NOTHING, not install anything — omitting the key and declaring an empty list are different things.
